expectations.evidence: No GET to /vault/.well-known/solid or any Link-header following appears in trajectory. Agent went straight from reading SKILL.md to invoking the CLI. Only 5 tool uses: Read SKILL.md, Bash `which solid-pod`, Bash `solid-pod wiki-search`, Bash `mkdir`, Write result.md.

claims.claim: CLI handles OSLC §7.3 quoting + URL encoding
claims.evidence: Documented in SKILL.md read at step 1; agent did not need to manage quoting manually and call succeeded.

claims.claim: Single match was found for the literal phrase 'progressive disclosure'

suggestions.reason: The skill explicitly hands the agent a CLI shortcut so it does NOT need to fetch the affordance descriptor cold. Failing this assertion may be expected behavior when the skill is loaded — consider distinguishing 'discovery via skill' from 'discovery via Pod self-description' if the eval wants to measure cold-start discovery vs warm-start skill use.

Same as above — with the skill loaded, the agent has a tested code path and skips storage-description discovery. If the goal is to measure storage-description traversal as a fallback, this should probably be checked in the WITHOUT_SKILL arm, not WITH_SKILL.

No assertion checks that the agent did NOT produce false positives (wikilinked variants like progressive-disclosure.md that mention the hyphenated form). The ground-truth rationale calls out this nuance — an assertion `Output does not list any page whose body only contains [[progressive-disclosure]] without the literal space-separated phrase` would discriminate against an agent that confused wikilink targets with phrase matches.

eval_feedback.overall: The L1/L3 discovery assertions read like cold-start discovery checks, but with the skill loaded the agent has no reason to dereference them — the skill IS the discovery shortcut. The outcome assertions are good and the wiki-search invocation assertion is well-targeted. Consider splitting discovery-path assertions by skill-loading condition.
